sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Ship, get profitable, raise from strength, and open everything
sections.para: A startup operating and investing model in three pillars. Ship something usable, give it away briefly, then take it away to see if anyone notices; be profitable before raising, so investors call you; and open source everything, because technology was never the moat. Each pillar buys the position needed for the next.

sections.label: Pillar one: ship something somebody can use
sections.line: Shipping means a usable product, not a demo
sections.para: A startup makes something people buy at a price profitable to you, so the key skill is shipping daily: a thing a stranger can use alone, however rough. Keep running costs near nothing with serverless and minimal state; here the file system is the database. Getting the product into strangers' hands is the first real product.

sections.label: Then give it away, and then take it away
sections.line: Give it away briefly, then check they miss it
sections.para: Offer the product free for a short window, which surfaces dozens of access and usability problems. Then deliberately take it away, without changing anything or apologising, and ask whether people miss it. A shrug means people only accept it while free, with no why now to sell; people coming back asking for it means you have something.

sections.label: Can you charge, and can you charge at a profit?
sections.line: Price must satisfy buyers and still be profitable
sections.para: Ask both whether buyers happily pay the price and whether it is profitable, allowing for a gap that scale will close if you can self fund it. Revenue comes first and profitability changes everything. Avoid default subscriptions: subscriptions.sgit.ai argues they are a discount for regular use, and pay on demand is usually healthier.

sections.label: Pillar two: the investors should be calling you
sections.line: Raise only after profitability, from a position of strength
sections.para: The worst time to raise is before profit, product or fit, when you bargain from weakness against a clock. Profit buys time, and the worst terms hand control to investors whose focus is misaligned, a common self-inflicted failure. As in music, do not sign before you have the album; raise from strength, on your terms.

sections.label: Pillar three: open source everything
sections.line: Open sourcing everything strengthens rather than gives away value
sections.para: Five reasons: technology is not the moat, so openness forces you to find what is defensible; code for strangers has cleaner architecture; open source normalises throwing things away; customers can read rather than trust; and founders keep their tools when they leave. Open source is a strategy, not a charity. A 2 October 2026 follow-up continues it.

sections.label: Why this is on a site about encrypted vaults
sections.line: Encrypted vaults make cheap, reversible shipping possible
sections.para: Every pillar needs shipping to be cheap, fast and reversible, which vaults provide: data, app, history and sources travel as one string with no database, hosting, account or install. The published estate is 2,662 files and 295 MB, opened with one read key. That loop, open source throughout, is what Dinis wants others to have.
